raw: AUGUST 15.

translation.en: August 15
translation.kr: 8월 15일

raw: There can be no doubt that in this world nothing is so indispensable as love. I observe that Charlotte could not lose me without a pang, and the very children have but one wish; that is, that I should visit them again to-morrow. I went this afternoon to tune Charlotte's piano. But I could not do it, for the little ones insisted on my telling them a story; and Charlotte herself urged me to satisfy them. I waited upon them at tea, and they are now as fully contented with me as with Charlotte; and I told them my very best tale of the princess who was waited upon by dwarfs. I improve myself by this exercise, and am quite surprised at the impression my stories create. If I sometimes invent an incident which I forget upon the next narration, they remind one directly that the story was different before; so that I now endeavour to relate with exactness the same anecdote in the same monotonous tone, which never changes. I find by this, how much an author injures his works by altering them, even though they be improved in a poetical point of view. The first impression is readily received. We are so constituted that we believe the most incredible things; and, once they are engraved upon the memory, woe to him who would endeavour to efface them.

translation.en: There can be no doubt that nothing in this world is so indispensable as love.
translation.kr: 이 세상에 사랑만큼 없어서는 안 될 것이 없다는 데에는 의심의 여지가 없네.

translation.en: I see that Charlotte could not lose me without a pang, and the children have only one wish — that I should come and visit them again tomorrow.
translation.kr: 샤를로테가 나를 잃으면 마음 아파하리라는 것을 나는 아네. 그리고 아이들의 소원은 단 하나, 내가 내일 또 놀러 오는 것뿐일세.

translation.en: I went this afternoon to tune Charlotte's piano.
translation.kr: 오늘 오후에는 샤를로테의 피아노를 조율하러 갔었네.

translation.en: But I could not manage it, because the little ones insisted on my telling them a story, and Charlotte herself urged me to satisfy them.
translation.kr: 그런데 그러지 못했네. 아이들이 이야기를 해 달라고 졸랐고, 샤를로테까지 아이들 소원을 들어주라고 했으니.

translation.en: I waited on them at tea, and they are now as fully contented with me as with Charlotte; and I told them my very best tale, of the princess who was waited on by dwarfs.
translation.kr: 나는 아이들에게 차를 따라 주었네. 이제 아이들은 샤를로테에게 그러듯 내게도 온전히 마음을 놓지. 그리고 내 이야기 가운데 가장 좋은 것, 난쟁이들의 시중을 받는 공주 이야기를 들려주었네.

translation.en: I improve by the exercise, and I am quite surprised at the impression my stories make.
translation.kr: 이렇게 자꾸 하다 보니 나도 늘고, 내 이야기가 남기는 인상에 스스로도 꽤 놀라네.

translation.en: If I sometimes invent an incident and then forget it the next time, they tell me at once that the story was different before.
translation.kr: 어쩌다 한 대목을 지어냈다가 다음번에 잊어버리면, 아이들은 곧바로 전에는 이야기가 달랐다고 일러 주네.

translation.en: So I now try to relate the same anecdote exactly, in the same unchanging tone.
translation.kr: 그래서 이제는 같은 이야기를 한결같은 가락으로 꼭 그대로 들려주려고 애쓰네.

translation.en: From this I see how much an author injures his work by altering it, even when the change is an improvement in a poetical sense.
translation.kr: 이 일로 나는 알게 되었네. 작가가 제 글을 고칠 때, 설령 시적으로는 나아지는 손질이라 해도 얼마나 글을 상하게 하는지를.

translation.en: The first impression is readily received.
translation.kr: 첫인상은 쉽게 받아들여지는 법일세.

translation.en: We are so made that we believe the most incredible things; and once they are engraved on the memory, woe to the man who tries to rub them out.
translation.kr: 우리는 더없이 믿기 어려운 것도 믿게끔 생겨먹었고, 그것이 한번 기억에 새겨지고 나면 그것을 지우려 드는 자에게 화가 있을진저.

raw: AUGUST 18.

translation.en: August 18
translation.kr: 8월 18일

raw: Must it ever be thus,—that the source of our happiness must also be the fountain of our misery? The full and ardent sentiment which animated my heart with the love of nature, overwhelming me with a torrent of delight, and which brought all paradise before me, has now become an insupportable torment, a demon which perpetually pursues and harasses me. When in bygone days I gazed from these rocks upon yonder mountains across the river, and upon the green, flowery valley before me, and saw all nature budding and bursting around; the hills clothed from foot to peak with tall, thick forest trees; the valleys in all their varied windings, shaded with the loveliest woods; and the soft river gliding along amongst the lisping reeds, mirroring the beautiful clouds which the soft evening breeze wafted across the sky,—when I heard the groves about me melodious with the music of birds, and saw the million swarms of insects dancing in the last golden beams of the sun, whose setting rays awoke the humming beetles from their grassy beds, whilst the subdued tumult around directed my attention to the ground, and I there observed the arid rock compelled to yield nutriment to the dry moss, whilst the heath flourished upon the barren sands below me, all this displayed to me the inner warmth which animates all nature, and filled and glowed within my heart. I felt myself exalted by this overflowing fulness to the perception of the Godhead, and the glorious forms of an infinite universe became visible to my soul! Stupendous mountains encompassed me, abysses yawned at my feet, and cataracts fell headlong down before me; impetuous rivers rolled through the plain, and rocks and mountains resounded from afar. In the depths of the earth I saw innumerable powers in motion, and multiplying to infinity; whilst upon its surface, and beneath the heavens, there teemed ten thousand varieties of living creatures. Everything around is alive with an infinite number of forms; while mankind fly for security to their petty houses, from the shelter of which they rule in their imaginations over the wide-extended universe. Poor fool! in whose petty estimation all things are little. From the inaccessible mountains, across the desert which no mortal foot has trod, far as the confines of the unknown ocean, breathes the spirit of the eternal Creator; and every atom to which he has given existence finds favour in his sight. Ah, how often at that time has the flight of a bird, soaring above my head, inspired me with the desire of being transported to the shores of the immeasurable waters, there to quaff the pleasures of life from the foaming goblet of the Infinite, and to partake, if but for a moment even, with the confined powers of my soul, the beatitude of that Creator who accomplishes all things in himself, and through himself!

translation.en: Must it always be so — that the source of our happiness must also be the fountain of our misery?
translation.kr: 언제나 이러해야만 하는가 — 우리 행복의 샘이 곧 우리 불행의 샘이기도 해야 하는가?

translation.en: The full, ardent feeling that once animated my heart with the love of nature, overwhelming me with a torrent of delight and bringing all paradise before me, has now become an unbearable torment, a demon that pursues and harasses me everywhere.
translation.kr: 한때 내 가슴을 자연에 대한 사랑으로 뛰게 하고, 기쁨의 격류로 나를 휩쓸며 온 낙원을 눈앞에 펼쳐 주던 그 벅찬 감정이, 이제는 견딜 수 없는 고문이 되어 어디서나 나를 쫓아다니며 괴롭히는 악령이 되었네.

translation.en: In days gone by I would gaze from these rocks at the mountains across the river, and at the green, flowering valley below me, and see all nature budding and breaking open around me.
translation.kr: 지난날 나는 이 바위에서 강 건너 산들을, 그리고 발아래 푸르고 꽃 핀 골짜기를 바라보며, 온 자연이 움트고 터져 나오는 것을 보았네.

translation.en: The hills were clothed from foot to summit with tall, thick forest trees.
translation.kr: 언덕은 기슭에서 꼭대기까지 크고 빽빽한 숲으로 덮여 있었네.

translation.en: The valleys in all their windings were shaded with the loveliest woods.
translation.kr: 굽이굽이 이어진 골짜기들은 더없이 아름다운 나무 그늘에 잠겨 있었지.

translation.en: And the soft river slid along among the whispering reeds, mirroring the beautiful clouds that the evening breeze carried across the sky.
translation.kr: 그리고 부드러운 강물이 속삭이는 갈대 사이를 미끄러지며, 저녁 바람이 하늘을 가로질러 실어 가는 고운 구름을 비추고 있었네.

translation.en: I heard the groves around me full of birdsong, and saw the million swarms of insects dancing in the last golden beams of the sun, whose setting rays woke the humming beetles out of their grassy beds.
translation.kr: 둘레의 숲은 새소리로 가득했고, 수없이 떼 지은 벌레들이 해의 마지막 금빛 속에서 춤추는 것을 보았네. 그 지는 빛살이 풀밭 잠자리에서 붕붕대는 딱정벌레들을 깨웠지.

translation.en: The subdued stir all around turned my attention to the ground, where I saw the arid rock forced to yield nourishment to the dry moss, and the heath flourishing on the barren sands below me.
translation.kr: 사방의 나직한 술렁임이 내 눈길을 땅으로 이끌었고, 거기서 나는 메마른 바위가 마른 이끼를 먹여 살리는 것을, 그리고 그 아래 척박한 모래밭에서 히스가 무성한 것을 보았네.

translation.en: All of it showed me the inner warmth that animates the whole of nature, and it filled my heart and glowed there.
translation.kr: 그 모든 것이 온 자연을 살아 움직이게 하는 안쪽의 온기를 내게 보여 주었고, 그것이 내 가슴을 채우고 거기서 타올랐네.

translation.en: I felt myself raised by this overflowing fullness to a perception of the Godhead, and the glorious forms of an infinite universe became visible to my soul.
translation.kr: 그 넘쳐 나는 충만함이 나를 들어 올려 신성을 감지하게 했고, 무한한 우주의 영광스러운 형상들이 내 영혼에 보이게 되었네.

translation.en: Stupendous mountains encircled me, abysses yawned at my feet, and cataracts fell headlong before me.
translation.kr: 엄청난 산들이 나를 에워쌌고, 발밑에는 심연이 입을 벌렸으며, 눈앞에서는 폭포가 곤두박질쳤네.

translation.en: Impetuous rivers rolled across the plain, and rocks and mountains echoed from far off.
translation.kr: 사나운 강들이 들판을 굴러갔고, 바위와 산이 멀리서 메아리쳤네.

translation.en: In the depths of the earth I saw innumerable powers in motion, multiplying to infinity; while on its surface, and under the heavens, ten thousand kinds of living creatures teemed.
translation.kr: 땅속 깊은 곳에서 나는 헤아릴 수 없는 힘들이 움직이며 끝없이 불어나는 것을 보았네. 그 지면 위에서는, 그리고 하늘 아래에서는 만 가지 생물이 우글거렸고.

translation.en: Everything around is alive with an infinite number of forms, while mankind flies for safety into its petty houses, and from that shelter rules in imagination over the whole wide universe.
translation.kr: 둘레의 모든 것이 무수한 형상으로 살아 있는데, 사람은 제 초라한 집으로 피해 들어가 그 안에서 상상으로 이 넓은 우주를 다스리고 있네.

translation.en: Poor fool, in whose small reckoning all things are small.
translation.kr: 가엾은 바보 같으니. 그 좁은 셈속에서는 무엇이든 다 작아지는구나.

translation.en: From the inaccessible mountains, across the desert no mortal foot has trodden, out to the edge of the unknown ocean, breathes the spirit of the eternal Creator; and every atom he has given existence to finds favour in his sight.
translation.kr: 다다를 수 없는 산에서, 사람의 발이 닿은 적 없는 사막을 건너, 알지 못하는 바다의 끝까지 영원한 창조주의 숨결이 불고 있네. 그리고 그가 존재를 준 티끌 하나하나가 그 눈에 사랑스러운 것일세.

translation.en: Ah, how often in those days the flight of a bird overhead filled me with the longing to be carried to the shores of the immeasurable waters.
translation.kr: 아, 그 시절 머리 위로 날아가는 새 한 마리가 얼마나 자주 나를 저 가없는 물가로 실려 가고 싶은 그리움으로 채웠던지.

translation.en: To drink the pleasures of life there from the foaming goblet of the Infinite.
translation.kr: 거기서 무한의 거품 이는 잔으로 삶의 기쁨을 들이켜고 싶은 그리움으로.

translation.en: And to share, if only for a moment, with the confined powers of my soul, the blessedness of that Creator who accomplishes all things in himself and through himself.
translation.kr: 그리고 좁디좁은 내 영혼의 힘으로나마, 단 한 순간만이라도, 만물을 제 안에서 제 힘으로 이루시는 그 창조주의 복됨을 나누고 싶은 그리움으로.

raw: My dear friend, the bare recollection of those hours still consoles me. Even this effort to recall those ineffable sensations, and give them utterance, exalts my soul above itself, and makes me doubly feel the intensity of my present anguish.

translation.en: My dear friend, the bare recollection of those hours still consoles me.
translation.kr: 친구여, 그 시간들을 떠올리는 것만으로도 아직 위로가 되네.

translation.en: Even this effort to recall those unspeakable sensations and put them into words raises my soul above itself, and makes me feel doubly the intensity of my present anguish.
translation.kr: 그 말로 다 할 수 없던 느낌들을 되살려 말로 옮기려는 이 애씀조차 내 영혼을 제 위로 들어 올리고, 지금 내 괴로움의 깊이를 곱절로 느끼게 하네.

raw: It is as if a curtain had been drawn from before my eyes, and, instead of prospects of eternal life, the abyss of an ever open grave yawned before me. Can we say of anything that it exists when all passes away, when time, with the speed of a storm, carries all things onward,—and our transitory existence, hurried along by the torrent, is either swallowed up by the waves or dashed against the rocks? There is not a moment but preys upon you,—and upon all around you, not a moment in which you do not yourself become a destroyer. The most innocent walk deprives of life thousands of poor insects: one step destroys the fabric of the industrious ant, and converts a little world into chaos. No: it is not the great and rare calamities of the world, the floods which sweep away whole villages, the earthquakes which swallow up our towns, that affect me. My heart is wasted by the thought of that destructive power which lies concealed in every part of universal nature. Nature has formed nothing that does not consume itself, and every object near it: so that, surrounded by earth and air, and all the active powers, I wander on my way with aching heart; and the universe is to me a fearful monster, for ever devouring its own offspring.

translation.en: It is as though a curtain had been drawn back from my eyes, and instead of the prospect of eternal life, the abyss of an ever-open grave yawned in front of me.
translation.kr: 내 눈앞에서 장막이 걷힌 듯하고, 영원한 생명의 전망 대신 언제나 입을 벌린 무덤의 심연이 앞에 놓여 있네.

translation.en: Can we say of anything that it exists, when everything passes away — when time, with the speed of a storm, carries all things onward, and our brief existence, swept along by the torrent, is either swallowed by the waves or dashed against the rocks?
translation.kr: 모든 것이 스러져 가는데 무엇이 존재한다고 말할 수 있겠나 — 시간이 폭풍 같은 속도로 만물을 실어 가고, 그 격류에 휩쓸린 우리의 짧은 삶이 물결에 삼켜지거나 바위에 부딪혀 부서지는데?

translation.en: There is not a moment that does not prey upon you and on everything around you; not a moment in which you do not yourself become a destroyer.
translation.kr: 자네와 자네 둘레의 모든 것을 갉아먹지 않는 순간은 하나도 없고, 자네 자신이 파괴자가 되지 않는 순간도 하나도 없네.

translation.en: The most innocent walk takes the lives of thousands of poor insects; one step wrecks the fabric of the industrious ant and turns a little world into chaos.
translation.kr: 더없이 무심한 산책 한 번이 가엾은 벌레 수천의 목숨을 앗아 가고, 한 걸음이 부지런한 개미의 집을 허물어 작은 세계를 혼돈으로 바꾸어 놓네.

translation.en: No: it is not the great and rare calamities of the world that move me — not the floods that sweep away whole villages, nor the earthquakes that swallow our towns.
translation.kr: 아니야, 나를 흔드는 것은 세상의 크고 드문 재앙이 아닐세 — 온 마을을 쓸어 가는 홍수도, 도시를 삼키는 지진도 아니네.

translation.en: My heart is wasted by the thought of that destructive power hidden in every part of universal nature.
translation.kr: 내 마음을 말려 죽이는 것은, 온 자연의 구석구석에 숨어 있는 그 파괴하는 힘에 대한 생각일세.

translation.en: Nature has formed nothing that does not consume itself and everything near it.
translation.kr: 자연이 지어낸 것 가운데 제 몸과 제 곁의 것을 함께 삼키지 않는 것은 하나도 없네.

translation.en: So, surrounded by earth and air and all the active powers, I go my way with an aching heart; and the universe is to me a fearful monster, for ever devouring its own offspring.
translation.kr: 그리하여 땅과 공기와 온갖 움직이는 힘에 둘러싸인 채, 나는 아픈 가슴으로 내 길을 가네. 그리고 우주는 내게 제 새끼를 끝없이 집어삼키는 무서운 괴물일세.

raw: AUGUST 21.

translation.en: August 21
translation.kr: 8월 21일

raw: In vain do I stretch out my arms toward her when I awaken in the morning from my weary slumbers. In vain do I seek for her at night in my bed, when some innocent dream has happily deceived me, and placed her near me in the fields, when I have seized her hand and covered it with countless kisses. And when I feel for her in the half confusion of sleep, with the happy sense that she is near, tears flow from my oppressed heart; and, bereft of all comfort, I weep over my future woes.

translation.en: In vain I stretch out my arms toward her when I wake in the morning from my weary sleep.
translation.kr: 고단한 잠에서 아침에 깨어 그 사람을 향해 팔을 뻗어 보아도 헛일일세.

translation.en: In vain I feel for her at night in my bed, when some innocent dream has happily deceived me and set her beside me in the fields, and I have seized her hand and covered it with countless kisses.
translation.kr: 순진한 꿈이 나를 다행히도 속여 들판에서 그 사람을 내 곁에 세워 주고 내가 그 손을 붙잡아 수없이 입 맞춘 뒤, 밤에 잠자리에서 그 사람을 더듬어 보아도 헛일일세.

translation.en: And when I reach for her in the half confusion of sleep, in the happy certainty that she is near, tears flow from my oppressed heart, and, robbed of all comfort, I weep over the sorrows still to come.
translation.kr: 그리고 잠결의 어렴풋함 속에서, 그 사람이 가까이 있다는 행복한 확신으로 손을 뻗을 때면, 짓눌린 가슴에서 눈물이 흘러나오고, 온갖 위로를 빼앗긴 채 나는 앞으로 올 슬픔을 두고 우네.

raw: AUGUST 22.

translation.en: August 22
translation.kr: 8월 22일

raw: What a misfortune, Wilhelm! My active spirits have degenerated into contented indolence. I cannot be idle, and yet I am unable to set to work. I cannot think: I have no longer any feeling for the beauties of nature, and books are distasteful to me. Once we give ourselves up, we are totally lost. Many a time and oft I wish I were a common labourer; that, awakening in the morning, I might have but one prospect, one pursuit, one hope, for the day which has dawned. I often envy Albert when I see him buried in a heap of papers and parchments, and I fancy I should be happy were I in his place. Often impressed with this feeling I have been on the point of writing to you and to the minister, for the appointment at the embassy, which you think I might obtain. I believe I might procure it. The minister has long shown a regard for me, and has frequently urged me to seek employment. It is the business of an hour only. Now and then the fable of the horse recurs to me. Weary of liberty, he suffered himself to be saddled and bridled, and was ridden to death for his pains. I know not what to determine upon. For is not this anxiety for change the consequence of that restless spirit which would pursue me equally in every situation of life?

translation.en: What a misfortune, Wilhelm!
translation.kr: 이 무슨 불행인가, 빌헬름!

translation.en: My active spirits have sunk into a contented indolence.
translation.kr: 활발하던 내 기운이 안일한 나태로 가라앉고 말았네.

translation.en: I cannot be idle, and yet I am unable to set to work.
translation.kr: 가만히 있지도 못하면서, 일에 손을 대지도 못하네.

translation.en: I cannot think; I have no feeling left for the beauties of nature, and books are distasteful to me.
translation.kr: 생각도 되지 않고, 자연의 아름다움에도 아무 느낌이 없으며, 책은 역겹네.

translation.en: Once we give ourselves up, we are lost entirely.
translation.kr: 한번 저를 놓아 버리면 우리는 아주 길을 잃고 마네.

translation.en: Many a time I wish I were a common labourer, so that on waking in the morning I might have one prospect, one pursuit, one hope for the day ahead.
translation.kr: 차라리 품팔이 일꾼이었으면 싶을 때가 많네. 아침에 눈을 뜨면 그날 하루에 바라볼 것 하나, 할 일 하나, 희망 하나가 있게 말일세.

translation.en: I often envy Albert when I see him buried in a heap of papers and parchments, and fancy I should be happy in his place.
translation.kr: 알베르트가 서류와 문서 더미에 파묻혀 있는 것을 보면 자주 부러워지고, 그 자리에 있으면 나도 행복하지 않을까 싶네.

translation.en: More than once, under that feeling, I have been on the point of writing to you and to the minister about the post at the embassy which you think I might obtain.
translation.kr: 그런 마음에 못 이겨, 자네가 얻을 수 있으리라 한 공사관 자리에 대해 자네와 장관께 편지를 쓸 뻔한 적이 한두 번이 아닐세.

translation.en: I believe I could get it.
translation.kr: 얻을 수 있으리라 생각하네.

translation.en: The minister has long shown a regard for me, and has often urged me to look for employment.
translation.kr: 장관은 오래전부터 나를 좋게 보아 왔고, 일자리를 알아보라고 여러 번 권했으니.

translation.en: It would be the business of an hour.
translation.kr: 한 시간이면 끝날 일이지.

translation.en: Now and then the fable of the horse comes back to me.
translation.kr: 그러다 문득 그 말에 관한 우화가 떠오르네.

translation.en: Weary of his liberty, he let himself be saddled and bridled, and was ridden to death for his pains.
translation.kr: 제 자유에 싫증이 난 말은 안장과 굴레를 받아들였고, 그 대가로 죽도록 부려졌다는 이야기 말일세.

translation.en: I do not know what to decide.
translation.kr: 나는 어떻게 정해야 할지 모르겠네.

translation.en: For is not this longing for change just the restless spirit that would follow me into any situation in life?
translation.kr: 게다가 이 변화에 대한 갈망이야말로, 어떤 처지에 놓이든 나를 따라다닐 그 들뜬 기질이 아니고 무엇이겠나?

raw: AUGUST 28.

translation.en: August 28
translation.kr: 8월 28일

raw: If my ills would admit of any cure, they would certainly be cured here. This is my birthday, and early in the morning I received a packet from Albert. Upon opening it, I found one of the pink ribbons which Charlotte wore in her dress the first time I saw her, and which I had several times asked her to give me. With it were two volumes in duodecimo of Wetstein's "Homer," a book I had often wished for, to save me the inconvenience of carrying the large Ernestine edition with me upon my walks. You see how they anticipate my wishes, how well they understand all those little attentions of friendship, so superior to the costly presents of the great, which are humiliating. I kissed the ribbon a thousand times, and in every breath inhaled the remembrance of those happy and irrevocable days which filled me with the keenest joy. Such, Wilhelm, is our fate. I do not murmur at it: the flowers of life are but visionary. How many pass away, and leave no trace behind—how few yield any fruit—and the fruit itself, how rarely does it ripen! And yet there are flowers enough! and is it not strange, my friend, that we should suffer the little that does really ripen, to rot, decay, and perish unenjoyed? Farewell! This is a glorious summer. I often climb into the trees in Charlotte's orchard, and shake down the pears that hang on the highest branches. She stands below, and catches them as they fall.

translation.en: If my troubles admitted of any cure, they would certainly be cured here.
translation.kr: 내 괴로움에 무슨 약이 있다면, 여기서라면 분명 나았을 걸세.

translation.en: This is my birthday, and early in the morning I received a packet from Albert.
translation.kr: 오늘은 내 생일인데, 이른 아침에 알베르트에게서 꾸러미가 하나 왔네.

translation.en: On opening it I found one of the pink ribbons Charlotte wore in her dress the first time I saw her, and which I had several times asked her to give me.
translation.kr: 열어 보니 처음 만난 날 샤를로테가 옷에 달고 있던, 그리고 내가 여러 번 달라고 졸랐던 그 분홍 리본이 들어 있었네.

translation.en: With it were two small volumes of Wetstein's "Homer," a book I had often wished for, to save me the trouble of carrying the large Ernestine edition on my walks.
translation.kr: 함께 베트슈타인판 "호메로스" 작은 두 권이 있었는데, 산책할 때 큰 에르네스티판을 들고 다니는 수고를 덜 수 있어 전부터 갖고 싶어 하던 책일세.

translation.en: You see how they anticipate my wishes, how well they understand those small attentions of friendship, so far above the costly presents of the great, which only humiliate.
translation.kr: 보게, 그들이 내 바람을 얼마나 먼저 알아채는지, 그 작은 우정의 배려를 얼마나 잘 아는지를. 사람을 초라하게 만드는 높은 분들의 값비싼 선물과는 견줄 수 없는 것이지.

translation.en: I kissed the ribbon a thousand times, and with every breath drew in the memory of those happy and irrecoverable days that filled me with the keenest joy.
translation.kr: 나는 그 리본에 천 번이나 입을 맞추었고, 숨을 쉴 때마다 더없이 큰 기쁨으로 나를 채웠던 그 행복하고 돌이킬 수 없는 날들의 기억을 들이마셨네.

translation.en: Such, Wilhelm, is our fate.
translation.kr: 빌헬름, 우리 운명이란 그런 것일세.

translation.en: I do not complain of it: the flowers of life are only apparitions.
translation.kr: 나는 그것을 원망하지 않네. 삶의 꽃이란 헛것일 뿐이니.

translation.en: How many pass away and leave no trace behind — how few yield any fruit — and the fruit itself, how rarely does it ripen!
translation.kr: 얼마나 많은 꽃이 자취도 없이 스러지는가 — 열매를 맺는 꽃은 또 얼마나 적은가 — 그리고 그 열매조차 얼마나 드물게 익는가!

translation.en: And yet there are flowers enough; and is it not strange, my friend, that we should let the little that does ripen rot and perish unenjoyed?
translation.kr: 그런데도 꽃은 넉넉하지. 그러니 친구여, 어렵게 익은 그 얼마 안 되는 것마저 우리가 맛보지도 않고 썩어 문드러지게 둔다는 것이 이상하지 않은가?

translation.en: Farewell!
translation.kr: 잘 있게!

translation.en: This is a glorious summer.
translation.kr: 눈부신 여름일세.

translation.en: I often climb into the trees in Charlotte's orchard and shake down the pears that hang on the highest branches.
translation.kr: 나는 자주 샤를로테네 과수원 나무에 올라가, 가장 높은 가지에 달린 배를 흔들어 떨어뜨리네.

translation.en: She stands below and catches them as they fall.
translation.kr: 그 사람은 아래 서서 떨어지는 것을 받네.

raw: AUGUST 30.

translation.en: August 30
translation.kr: 8월 30일

raw: Unhappy being that I am! Why do I thus deceive myself? What is to come of all this wild, aimless, endless passion? I cannot pray except to her. My imagination sees nothing but her: all surrounding objects are of no account, except as they relate to her. In this dreamy state I enjoy many happy hours, till at length I feel compelled to tear myself away from her. Ah, Wilhelm, to what does not my heart often compel me! When I have spent several hours in her company, till I feel completely absorbed by her figure, her grace, the divine expression of her thoughts, my mind becomes gradually excited to the highest excess, my sight grows dim, my hearing confused, my breathing oppressed as if by the hand of a murderer, and my beating heart seeks to obtain relief for my aching senses. I am sometimes unconscious whether I really exist. If in such moments I find no sympathy, and Charlotte does not allow me to enjoy the melancholy consolation of bathing her hand with my tears, I feel compelled to tear myself from her, when I either wander through the country, climb some precipitous cliff, or force a path through the trackless thicket, where I am lacerated and torn by thorns and briers; and thence I find relief. Sometimes I lie stretched on the ground, overcome with fatigue and dying with thirst; sometimes, late in the night, when the moon shines above me, I recline against an aged tree in some sequestered forest, to rest my weary limbs, when, exhausted and worn, I sleep till break of day. O Wilhelm! the hermit's cell, his sackcloth, and girdle of thorns would be luxury and indulgence compared with what I suffer. Adieu! I see no end to this wretchedness except the grave.

translation.en: Unhappy creature that I am!
translation.kr: 나는 얼마나 불행한 인간인가!

translation.en: Why do I deceive myself like this?
translation.kr: 어찌하여 나는 이렇게 나를 속이고 있는가?

translation.en: What is to come of all this wild, aimless, endless passion?
translation.kr: 이 거칠고 갈 곳 없고 끝없는 정념에서 무엇이 나오겠는가?

translation.en: I can pray to no one but her.
translation.kr: 나는 그 사람 말고는 누구에게도 기도할 수 없네.

translation.en: My imagination sees nothing but her; everything around me counts for nothing except as it relates to her.
translation.kr: 내 상상에는 그 사람밖에 보이지 않고, 둘레의 모든 것은 그 사람과 관련될 때에만 뜻이 있네.

translation.en: In this dreaming state I enjoy many happy hours, until at last I feel forced to tear myself away from her.
translation.kr: 이렇게 꿈꾸는 상태에서 나는 행복한 시간을 많이 누리다가, 마침내 억지로 그 사람에게서 나를 떼어 내야만 하네.

translation.en: Ah, Wilhelm, what does my heart not drive me to!
translation.kr: 아, 빌헬름, 내 마음이 나를 어디까지 몰아가는지!

translation.en: When I have spent several hours in her company, until I am completely absorbed by her figure, her grace, the divine expression of her thoughts, my mind works itself up to the highest pitch.
translation.kr: 그 곁에서 몇 시간을 보내다 그 자태와 우아함과 생각의 거룩한 표정에 온전히 잠겨 버리면, 내 마음은 극도로 달아오르네.

translation.en: My sight grows dim, my hearing confused, my breathing tightens as though a murderer's hand were on my throat, and my beating heart tries to find relief for my aching senses.
translation.kr: 눈앞이 흐려지고 귀가 먹먹해지며, 살인자의 손이 목을 누르는 듯 숨이 막히고, 뛰는 심장은 아픈 감각들을 달랠 길을 찾아 헤매네.

translation.en: Sometimes I do not know whether I really exist.
translation.kr: 때로는 내가 정말 존재하는지조차 모르겠네.

translation.en: If at such moments I find no sympathy, and Charlotte will not let me have the melancholy consolation of bathing her hand with my tears, I have to tear myself away from her.
translation.kr: 그런 순간에 아무 공감도 얻지 못하고, 샤를로테가 그 손을 내 눈물로 적시는 그 서글픈 위안조차 허락하지 않으면, 나는 그 사람에게서 나를 떼어 내야만 하네.

translation.en: Then I wander through the country, climb some steep cliff, or force a path through the trackless thicket, where the thorns and briers tear me — and there I find relief.
translation.kr: 그러고는 들판을 헤매거나 가파른 벼랑을 오르거나, 길도 없는 덤불을 헤치고 나아가 가시와 찔레에 살갗을 찢기네 — 그러면 마음이 놓이지.

translation.en: Sometimes I lie stretched on the ground, worn out with fatigue and dying of thirst.
translation.kr: 때로는 지치고 목이 타 땅바닥에 길게 뻗어 눕네.

translation.en: Sometimes, late in the night, with the moon above me, I lean against an old tree in some remote forest to rest my weary limbs, and, exhausted, sleep there till daybreak.
translation.kr: 때로는 깊은 밤 달을 이고, 외딴 숲의 늙은 나무에 기대어 고단한 몸을 쉬다가 기진해 날이 밝을 때까지 잠들기도 하네.

translation.en: O Wilhelm, the hermit's cell, his sackcloth and his girdle of thorns would be luxury and indulgence beside what I suffer.
translation.kr: 아, 빌헬름. 은수자의 굴과 그 삼베옷과 가시 띠도 내가 겪는 것에 견주면 호사요 방종일세.

translation.en: Adieu!
translation.kr: 잘 있게!

translation.en: I see no end to this wretchedness but the grave.
translation.kr: 이 비참함에 무덤 말고는 끝이 보이지 않네.

raw: SEPTEMBER 3.

translation.en: September 3
translation.kr: 9월 3일

raw: I must away. Thank you, Wilhelm, for determining my wavering purpose. For a whole fortnight I have thought of leaving her. I must away. She has returned to town, and is at the house of a friend. And then, Albert—yes, I must go.

translation.en: I must go.
translation.kr: 나는 떠나야겠네.

translation.en: Thank you, Wilhelm, for settling my wavering purpose.
translation.kr: 고맙네, 빌헬름. 흔들리던 내 마음을 자네가 잡아 주었네.

translation.en: For a whole fortnight I have been thinking of leaving her.
translation.kr: 꼬박 두 주 동안 그 사람을 두고 떠날 생각을 해 왔네.

translation.en: I must go.
translation.kr: 나는 떠나야겠네.

translation.en: She has gone back to town, and is staying at a friend's house.
translation.kr: 그 사람은 마을로 돌아가 친구 집에 머물고 있네.

translation.en: And then there is Albert — yes, I must go.
translation.kr: 게다가 알베르트가 있지 — 그래, 나는 떠나야겠네.

raw: SEPTEMBER 10.

translation.en: September 10
translation.kr: 9월 10일

raw: Oh, what a night, Wilhelm! I can henceforth bear anything. I shall never see her again. Oh, why cannot I fall on your neck, and, with floods of tears and raptures, give utterance to all the passions which distract my heart! Here I sit gasping for breath, and struggling to compose myself. I wait for day, and at sunrise the horses are to be at the door.

translation.en: Oh, what a night, Wilhelm!
translation.kr: 아, 얼마나 기막힌 밤이었는지, 빌헬름!

translation.en: After this I can bear anything.
translation.kr: 이제 나는 무엇이든 견딜 수 있네.

translation.en: I shall never see her again.
translation.kr: 나는 그 사람을 다시는 보지 못할 걸세.

translation.en: Oh, why can I not fall on your neck and pour out, in floods of tears and raptures, all the passions that tear at my heart!
translation.kr: 아, 어찌하여 나는 자네 목에 매달려, 눈물과 환희의 홍수 속에 내 가슴을 찢는 온갖 정념을 쏟아 낼 수 없는가!

translation.en: Here I sit gasping for breath, struggling to compose myself.
translation.kr: 여기 앉아 숨을 헐떡이며 마음을 가라앉히려 애쓰고 있네.

translation.en: I am waiting for daylight; at sunrise the horses are to be at the door.
translation.kr: 날이 밝기를 기다리네. 해가 뜨면 말이 문 앞에 와 있을 걸세.

raw: And she is sleeping calmly, little suspecting that she has seen me for the last time. I am free. I have had the courage, in an interview of two hours' duration, not to betray my intention. And O Wilhelm, what a conversation it was!

translation.en: And she is sleeping calmly, never suspecting that she has seen me for the last time.
translation.kr: 그리고 그 사람은 고이 잠들어 있네. 나를 마지막으로 보았다는 것은 꿈에도 모른 채.

translation.en: I am free.
translation.kr: 나는 자유롭네.

translation.en: I had the courage, through two hours of conversation, not to betray my intention.
translation.kr: 두 시간 동안 이야기를 나누면서도 내 뜻을 드러내지 않을 용기가 내게 있었네.

translation.en: And O Wilhelm, what a conversation it was!
translation.kr: 그리고 아, 빌헬름, 그것이 어떤 이야기였는지!

raw: Albert had promised to come to Charlotte in the garden immediately after supper. I was upon the terrace under the tall chestnut trees, and watched the setting sun. I saw him sink for the last time beneath this delightful valley and silent stream. I had often visited the same spot with Charlotte, and witnessed that glorious sight; and now—I was walking up and down the very avenue which was so dear to me. A secret sympathy had frequently drawn me thither before I knew Charlotte; and we were delighted when, in our early acquaintance, we discovered that we each loved the same spot, which is indeed as romantic as any that ever captivated the fancy of an artist.

translation.en: Albert had promised to join Charlotte in the garden immediately after supper.
translation.kr: 알베르트는 저녁을 먹고 곧바로 뜰에서 샤를로테와 만나기로 되어 있었네.

translation.en: I was on the terrace under the tall chestnut trees, watching the setting sun.
translation.kr: 나는 키 큰 밤나무 아래 테라스에서 지는 해를 바라보고 있었네.

translation.en: I saw him sink for the last time below this lovely valley and its silent stream.
translation.kr: 이 사랑스러운 골짜기와 고요한 시내 아래로 해가 마지막으로 잠기는 것을 보았네.

translation.en: I had often stood on that spot with Charlotte and watched that glorious sight; and now I was walking up and down the very avenue that was so dear to me.
translation.kr: 그 자리에서 샤를로테와 함께 그 눈부신 광경을 본 적이 여러 번이었네. 그런데 이제 나는 그토록 정든 바로 그 오솔길을 홀로 오가고 있었네.

translation.en: A secret sympathy had often drawn me there before I ever knew Charlotte; and we were delighted, early in our acquaintance, to discover that we both loved the same spot, which is as romantic as any that ever caught an artist's fancy.
translation.kr: 샤를로테를 알기 전부터 어떤 은밀한 이끌림이 나를 자주 그곳으로 데려갔었네. 그리고 알고 지낸 지 얼마 되지 않아 우리 둘 다 같은 자리를 좋아한다는 것을 알고 기뻐했었지. 화가의 마음을 사로잡을 만큼 그림 같은 곳이니 말일세.

raw: From beneath the chestnut trees, there is an extensive view. But I remember that I have mentioned all this in a former letter, and have described the tall mass of beech trees at the end, and how the avenue grows darker and darker as it winds its way among them, till it ends in a gloomy recess, which has all the charm of a mysterious solitude. I still remember the strange feeling of melancholy which came over me the first time I entered that dark retreat, at bright midday. I felt some secret foreboding that it would, one day, be to me the scene of some happiness or misery.

translation.en: From beneath the chestnut trees there is a wide view.
translation.kr: 밤나무 아래에서는 멀리까지 내다보이네.

translation.en: But I remember I have described all this in an earlier letter — the tall mass of beech trees at the end, and how the avenue grows darker and darker as it winds among them, until it ends in a gloomy recess that has all the charm of a mysterious solitude.
translation.kr: 그러나 이 이야기는 앞선 편지에 다 적었던 것 같네 — 끝자락의 우람한 너도밤나무 숲과, 그 사이를 굽이돌며 점점 어두워지다가 마침내 신비로운 고독의 매력을 온전히 지닌 침침한 후미진 자리로 끝나는 그 길 말일세.

translation.en: I still remember the strange melancholy that came over me the first time I stepped into that dark retreat, at bright midday.
translation.kr: 환한 대낮에 그 어두운 은신처에 처음 발을 들였을 때 나를 덮쳤던 그 기이한 우수를 나는 아직도 기억하네.

translation.en: I had some secret foreboding that it would one day be the scene of great happiness or great misery for me.
translation.kr: 언젠가 그곳이 내게 크나큰 행복이나 크나큰 불행의 무대가 되리라는 은밀한 예감이 들었었지.

raw: I had spent half an hour struggling between the contending thoughts of going and returning, when I heard them coming up the terrace. I ran to meet them. I trembled as I took her hand, and kissed it. As we reached the top of the terrace, the moon rose from behind the wooded hill. We conversed on many subjects, and, without perceiving it, approached the gloomy recess. Charlotte entered, and sat down. Albert seated himself beside her. I did the same, but my agitation did not suffer me to remain long seated. I got up, and stood before her, then walked backward and forward, and sat down again. I was restless and miserable. Charlotte drew our attention to the beautiful effect of the moonlight, which threw a silver hue over the terrace in front of us, beyond the beech trees. It was a glorious sight, and was rendered more striking by the darkness which surrounded the spot where we were. We remained for some time silent, when Charlotte observed, "Whenever I walk by moonlight, it brings to my remembrance all my beloved and departed friends, and I am filled with thoughts of death and futurity. We shall live again, Werther!" she continued, with a firm but feeling voice; "but shall we know one another again—what do you think? what do you say?"

translation.en: I had spent half an hour torn between the thought of going and the thought of staying, when I heard them coming up the terrace.
translation.kr: 가느냐 머무느냐 사이에서 반 시간을 헤매고 있는데, 그들이 테라스로 올라오는 소리가 들렸네.

translation.en: I ran to meet them.
translation.kr: 나는 달려 나가 맞았네.

translation.en: I trembled as I took her hand and kissed it.
translation.kr: 그 손을 잡아 입을 맞출 때 나는 떨었네.

translation.en: As we reached the top of the terrace, the moon rose from behind the wooded hill.
translation.kr: 우리가 테라스 위쪽에 이르자, 숲이 우거진 언덕 뒤에서 달이 떠올랐네.

translation.en: We talked of many things, and without noticing it came to the gloomy recess.
translation.kr: 우리는 여러 이야기를 나누었고, 어느새 그 침침한 후미진 자리에 이르렀네.

translation.en: Charlotte went in and sat down.
translation.kr: 샤를로테가 들어가 앉았네.

translation.en: Albert seated himself beside her.
translation.kr: 알베르트가 그 곁에 앉았네.

translation.en: I did the same, but my agitation would not let me sit for long.
translation.kr: 나도 앉았네만, 마음이 들떠 오래 앉아 있지 못했네.

translation.en: I got up and stood in front of her, then walked back and forth, then sat down again.
translation.kr: 일어나 그 앞에 섰다가, 이리저리 거닐다가, 다시 앉았네.

translation.en: I was restless and miserable.
translation.kr: 나는 안절부절못했고 비참했네.

translation.en: Charlotte drew our attention to the beautiful effect of the moonlight, which threw a silver hue over the terrace in front of us, beyond the beech trees.
translation.kr: 샤를로테가 우리에게 달빛의 고운 자취를 가리켜 보였네. 너도밤나무 너머 우리 앞 테라스에 은빛이 깔려 있었지.

translation.en: It was a glorious sight, made more striking by the darkness that surrounded the spot where we sat.
translation.kr: 눈부신 광경이었고, 우리가 앉은 자리를 둘러싼 어둠이 그것을 더욱 도드라지게 했네.

translation.en: We were silent for a while, and then Charlotte said, "Whenever I walk by moonlight, it brings back to me all my beloved and departed friends, and I am filled with thoughts of death and of what is to come."
translation.kr: 한동안 말이 없다가 샤를로테가 말했네. "달빛 속을 걸을 때면 언제나 사랑했던 이들, 세상을 떠난 이들이 다 떠올라요. 그리고 죽음과 앞으로 올 것에 대한 생각으로 가득해지지요."

translation.en: "We shall live again, Werther!" she went on, in a firm but feeling voice. "But shall we know one another again? What do you think? What do you say?"
translation.kr: "우리는 다시 살게 될 거예요, 베르테르!" 그 사람은 굳으면서도 떨리는 목소리로 말을 이었네. "그런데 우리가 서로를 알아볼 수 있을까요? 어떻게 생각하세요? 무어라 말씀하시겠어요?"

raw: "Charlotte," I said, as I took her hand in mine, and my eyes filled with tears, "we shall see each other again—here and hereafter we shall meet again." I could say no more. Why, Wilhelm, should she put this question to me, just at the moment when the fear of our cruel separation filled my heart?

translation.en: "Charlotte," I said, taking her hand in mine, my eyes filling with tears, "we shall see each other again — here and hereafter we shall meet again."
translation.kr: "샤를로테." 나는 그 손을 내 손에 잡고, 눈에 눈물이 고인 채 말했네. "우리는 다시 만날 것입니다 — 이승에서도 저승에서도 다시 만날 것입니다."

translation.en: I could say no more.
translation.kr: 나는 더 말하지 못했네.

translation.en: Why, Wilhelm, should she put that question to me, just at the moment when the fear of our cruel separation filled my heart?
translation.kr: 빌헬름, 어찌하여 그 사람은 하필 그 순간에, 우리의 모진 이별에 대한 두려움이 내 가슴을 가득 채운 바로 그때 그런 물음을 던졌을까?

raw: "And oh! do those departed ones know how we are employed here? do they know when we are well and happy? do they know when we recall their memories with the fondest love? In the silent hour of evening the shade of my mother hovers around me; when seated in the midst of my children, I see them assembled near me, as they used to assemble near her; and then I raise my anxious eyes to heaven, and wish she could look down upon us, and witness how I fulfil the promise I made to her in her last moments, to be a mother to her children. With what emotion do I then exclaim, 'Pardon, dearest of mothers, pardon me, if I do not adequately supply your place! Alas! I do my utmost. They are clothed and fed; and, still better, they are loved and educated. Could you but see, sweet saint! the peace and harmony that dwells amongst us, you would glorify God with the warmest feelings of gratitude, to whom, in your last hour, you addressed such fervent prayers for our happiness.'" Thus did she express herself; but O Wilhelm! who can do justice to her language? how can cold and passionless words convey the heavenly expressions of the spirit? Albert interrupted her gently. "This affects you too deeply, my dear Charlotte. I know your soul dwells on such recollections with intense delight; but I implore—" "O Albert!" she continued, "I am sure you do not forget the evenings when we three used to sit at the little round table, when papa was absent, and the little ones had retired. You often had a good book with you, but seldom read it; the conversation of that noble being was preferable to everything,—that beautiful, bright, gentle, and yet ever-toiling woman. God alone knows how I have supplicated with tears on my nightly couch, that I might be like her."

translation.en: "And oh, do those who have gone know how we spend our time here? Do they know when we are well and happy? Do they know when we call up their memory with the fondest love?"
translation.kr: "아, 떠난 이들은 우리가 여기서 어떻게 지내는지 알까요? 우리가 잘 지내고 행복한 때를 알까요? 우리가 더없이 애틋한 마음으로 그들을 떠올리는 때를 알까요?"

translation.en: "In the silent hour of evening the shade of my mother hovers around me."
translation.kr: "고요한 저녁이면 어머니의 그림자가 내 둘레를 맴돌아요."

translation.en: "When I sit among my children and see them gathered near me as they used to gather near her, I raise my anxious eyes to heaven and wish she could look down on us, and see how I keep the promise I made her in her last moments, to be a mother to her children."
translation.kr: "아이들 틈에 앉아, 그 애들이 예전에 어머니 곁에 모이던 것처럼 내 곁에 모인 것을 보면, 나는 애타는 눈으로 하늘을 우러러 바라지요. 어머니가 우리를 내려다보시고, 마지막 순간에 그 아이들의 어머니가 되겠다고 드린 약속을 내가 어떻게 지키고 있는지 보아 주셨으면 하고요."

translation.en: "With what feeling I then cry out: 'Pardon me, dearest of mothers, pardon me if I do not fill your place as I should!'"
translation.kr: "그때 어떤 심정으로 이렇게 외치는지 몰라요. '용서하세요, 세상에서 가장 사랑하는 어머니. 어머니 자리를 마땅히 채우지 못한다면 용서해 주세요!'"

translation.en: "Alas, I do my utmost."
translation.kr: "아, 저는 있는 힘을 다하고 있어요."

translation.en: "They are clothed and fed; and, better still, they are loved and brought up."
translation.kr: "아이들은 입고 먹습니다. 그보다 더한 것은, 사랑받고 자라고 있다는 것이지요."

translation.en: "Could you but see, sweet saint, the peace and harmony we live in, you would glorify God with the warmest gratitude — the God to whom, in your last hour, you prayed so fervently for our happiness.'"
translation.kr: "어머니, 우리가 사는 이 평화와 화목을 보실 수만 있다면, 더없이 뜨거운 감사로 하느님을 찬양하실 거예요. 마지막 시간에 우리 행복을 위해 그토록 간절히 기도드리던 그 하느님을요.'"

translation.en: So she spoke; but O Wilhelm, who can do justice to her words?
translation.kr: 그 사람은 그렇게 말했네. 그러나 아, 빌헬름, 누가 그 말을 제대로 옮길 수 있겠나?

translation.en: How can cold and passionless language convey the heavenly expression of a spirit?
translation.kr: 차갑고 메마른 말이 어떻게 한 영혼의 천상 같은 표정을 전할 수 있겠나?

translation.en: Albert interrupted her gently.
translation.kr: 알베르트가 부드럽게 말을 가로막았네.

translation.en: "This affects you too deeply, my dear Charlotte. I know your soul dwells on such recollections with intense delight; but I beg you —"
translation.kr: "당신에게 너무 깊이 사무치는 이야기요, 사랑하는 샤를로테. 그런 기억에 당신 마음이 얼마나 깊이 잠기는지 나도 아오. 그러나 부디 —"

translation.en: "O Albert," she went on, "I am sure you have not forgotten the evenings when the three of us used to sit at the little round table, when papa was away and the little ones had gone to bed."
translation.kr: "아, 알베르트." 그 사람이 말을 이었네. "아버지가 안 계시고 어린것들이 잠자리에 든 저녁이면 우리 셋이 작은 둥근 탁자에 둘러앉곤 했던 것, 당신도 잊지 않으셨겠지요."

translation.en: "You often had a good book with you, but you seldom read it; the conversation of that noble creature was better than anything — that beautiful, bright, gentle, and yet ever-toiling woman."
translation.kr: "당신은 좋은 책을 가져오시고도 거의 읽지 않으셨어요. 그 고결한 분과 나누는 이야기가 무엇보다 좋았으니까요 — 아름답고 밝고 부드러우면서도 늘 부지런했던 그분과요."

translation.en: "God alone knows how often I have begged with tears on my bed at night that I might be like her."
translation.kr: "밤마다 잠자리에서 그분처럼 되게 해 달라고 눈물로 얼마나 빌었는지는 하느님만 아세요."

raw: I threw myself at her feet, and, seizing her hand, bedewed it with a thousand tears. "Charlotte!" I exclaimed, "God's blessing and your mother's spirit are upon you." "Oh! that you had known her," she said, with a warm pressure of the hand. "She was worthy of being known to you." I thought I should have fainted: never had I received praise so flattering. She continued, "And yet she was doomed to die in the flower of her youth, when her youngest child was scarcely six months old. Her illness was but short, but she was calm and resigned; and it was only for her children, especially the youngest, that she felt unhappy. When her end drew nigh, she bade me bring them to her. I obeyed. The younger ones knew nothing of their approaching loss, while the elder ones were quite overcome with grief. They stood around the bed; and she raised her feeble hands to heaven, and prayed over them; then, kissing them in turn, she dismissed them, and said to me, 'Be you a mother to them.' I gave her my hand. 'You are promising much, my child,' she said: 'a mother's fondness and a mother's care! I have often witnessed, by your tears of gratitude, that you know what is a mother's tenderness: show it to your brothers and sisters, and be dutiful and faithful to your father as a wife; you will be his comfort.' She inquired for him. He had retired to conceal his intolerable anguish,—he was heartbroken, 'Albert, you were in the room.' She heard some one moving: she inquired who it was, and desired you to approach. She surveyed us both with a look of composure and satisfaction, expressive of her conviction that we should be happy,—happy with one another." Albert fell upon her neck, and kissed her, and exclaimed, "We are so, and we shall be so!" Even Albert, generally so tranquil, had quite lost his composure; and I was excited beyond expression.

translation.en: I threw myself at her feet, seized her hand, and wet it with a thousand tears.
translation.kr: 나는 그 발치에 몸을 던져 손을 붙잡고 천 방울 눈물로 적셨네.

translation.en: "Charlotte!" I exclaimed. "God's blessing and your mother's spirit are upon you."
translation.kr: "샤를로테!" 하고 나는 외쳤네. "하느님의 축복과 어머님의 영혼이 당신 위에 있습니다."

translation.en: "Oh, that you had known her," she said, pressing my hand warmly.
translation.kr: "아, 당신이 그분을 아셨더라면." 그 사람이 내 손을 꼭 쥐며 말했네.

translation.en: "She was worthy of being known to you."
translation.kr: "당신이 아실 만한 분이었어요."

translation.en: I thought I should faint; never had I been given praise so flattering.
translation.kr: 나는 기절할 것만 같았네. 그토록 기쁜 칭찬을 들어 본 적이 없었으니.

translation.en: She went on: "And yet she was doomed to die in the flower of her youth, when her youngest child was barely six months old."
translation.kr: 그 사람이 말을 이었네. "그런데도 그분은 한창때에 돌아가셔야 했어요. 막내가 겨우 여섯 달이었을 때지요."

translation.en: "Her illness was short, but she was calm and resigned; it was only for her children, and above all the youngest, that she was unhappy."
translation.kr: "앓으신 기간은 짧았고, 그분은 담담하고 차분하셨어요. 다만 아이들, 무엇보다 막내 때문에만 마음이 편치 않으셨지요."

translation.en: "When her end drew near, she told me to bring them to her."
translation.kr: "마지막이 가까워지자 아이들을 데려오라고 하셨어요."

translation.en: "I obeyed."
translation.kr: "나는 그대로 했지요."

translation.en: "The younger ones knew nothing of what was coming, while the elder ones were quite overcome with grief."
translation.kr: "어린것들은 무슨 일이 닥치는지 몰랐고, 큰 아이들은 슬픔에 겨워 어쩔 줄을 몰랐어요."

translation.en: "They stood around the bed, and she raised her feeble hands to heaven and prayed over them; then, kissing each in turn, she sent them away and said to me, 'Be a mother to them.'"
translation.kr: "아이들이 침대 둘레에 서자, 그분은 힘없는 두 손을 하늘로 들어 아이들을 위해 기도하셨어요. 그러고는 한 아이씩 입을 맞추고 내보내신 뒤 내게 말씀하셨지요. '네가 이 아이들의 어머니가 되어 다오.'"

translation.en: "I gave her my hand. 'You are promising a great deal, my child,' she said, 'a mother's fondness and a mother's care!'"
translation.kr: "나는 손을 드렸어요. '큰 약속을 하는구나, 얘야.' 그분이 말씀하셨어요. '어머니의 사랑과 어머니의 보살핌이란다!'"

translation.en: "'I have often seen, by your tears of gratitude, that you know what a mother's tenderness is. Show it to your brothers and sisters; and be as dutiful and faithful to your father as a wife would be. You will be his comfort.'"
translation.kr: "'네 고마움의 눈물을 보며 나는 여러 번 알았다. 네가 어머니의 다정함이 무엇인지 안다는 것을. 그것을 동생들에게 베풀어라. 그리고 아버지께는 아내가 그러하듯 효성스럽고 한결같아라. 네가 그분의 위로가 될 게다.'"

translation.en: "She asked for him. He had gone out to hide his unbearable anguish; he was heartbroken. 'Albert, you were in the room.'"
translation.kr: "그분이 아버지를 찾으셨어요. 아버지는 견딜 수 없는 괴로움을 감추려고 밖에 나가 계셨지요. 가슴이 무너지셨던 거예요. '알베르트, 당신은 그 방에 계셨지요.'"

translation.en: "She heard someone moving, asked who it was, and called you over."
translation.kr: "그분은 누가 움직이는 소리를 듣고 누구냐고 물으시더니, 당신을 불러들이셨어요."

translation.en: "She looked at us both with an expression of composure and satisfaction, as if certain that we should be happy — happy with one another."
translation.kr: "그리고 우리 둘을 바라보셨어요. 우리가 행복하리라는 것을, 서로와 함께 행복하리라는 것을 확신하신 듯 차분하고 흡족한 얼굴로요."

translation.en: Albert fell on her neck and kissed her, and cried, "We are, and we shall be!"
translation.kr: 알베르트는 그 목에 매달려 입을 맞추며 외쳤네. "우리는 행복하오. 앞으로도 그럴 것이오!"

translation.en: Even Albert, usually so tranquil, had quite lost his composure; and I was moved beyond words.
translation.kr: 늘 그토록 차분하던 알베르트조차 아주 평정을 잃었고, 나는 말로 다 할 수 없이 흔들렸네.

raw: "And such a being," She continued, "was to leave us, Werther! Great God, must we thus part with everything we hold dear in this world? Nobody felt this more acutely than the children: they cried and lamented for a long time afterward, complaining that men had carried away their dear mamma."

translation.en: "And such a being," she went on, "had to leave us, Werther!"
translation.kr: "그런 분이" 하고 그 사람이 말을 이었네. "우리를 떠나야 했어요, 베르테르!"

translation.en: "Great God, must we part like this with everything we hold dear in this world?"
translation.kr: "위대하신 하느님, 우리는 이 세상에서 소중히 여기는 모든 것과 이렇게 헤어져야만 하나요?"

translation.en: "Nobody felt it more keenly than the children: they cried and lamented for a long time afterwards, complaining that men had carried away their dear mamma."
translation.kr: "그것을 가장 사무치게 느낀 것은 아이들이었어요. 오래도록 울며 슬퍼하면서, 사람들이 사랑하는 엄마를 데려가 버렸다고 했지요."

raw: Charlotte rose. It aroused me; but I continued sitting, and held her hand. "Let us go," she said: "it grows late." She attempted to withdraw her hand: I held it still. "We shall see each other again," I exclaimed: "we shall recognise each other under every possible change! I am going," I continued, "going willingly; but, should I say for ever, perhaps I may not keep my word. Adieu, Charlotte; adieu, Albert. We shall meet again." "Yes: tomorrow, I think," she answered with a smile. Tomorrow! how I felt the word! Ah! she little thought, when she drew her hand away from mine. They walked down the avenue. I stood gazing after them in the moonlight. I threw myself upon the ground, and wept: I then sprang up, and ran out upon the terrace, and saw, under the shade of the linden-trees, her white dress disappearing near the garden-gate. I stretched out my arms, and she vanished.

translation.en: Charlotte rose.
translation.kr: 샤를로테가 일어섰네.

translation.en: It roused me; but I stayed sitting and held her hand.
translation.kr: 그 바람에 나도 정신이 들었네만, 그대로 앉아 그 손을 잡고 있었네.

translation.en: "Let us go," she said. "It is growing late."
translation.kr: "이만 가요." 그 사람이 말했네. "늦었어요."

translation.en: She tried to draw her hand away; I held it still.
translation.kr: 손을 빼려 하기에 나는 놓지 않았네.

translation.en: "We shall see each other again," I cried. "We shall know each other through any change!"
translation.kr: "우리는 다시 만날 것입니다." 나는 외쳤네. "어떻게 변하든 서로를 알아볼 것입니다!"

translation.en: "I am going," I went on, "going willingly; but if I said for ever, perhaps I should not keep my word."
translation.kr: "저는 갑니다." 나는 말을 이었네. "기꺼이 갑니다. 그러나 영영이라고 말한다면, 아마 그 말을 지키지 못할 것입니다."

translation.en: "Adieu, Charlotte; adieu, Albert."
translation.kr: "안녕히, 샤를로테. 안녕히, 알베르트."

translation.en: "We shall meet again."
translation.kr: "우리는 다시 만날 것입니다."

translation.en: "Yes — tomorrow, I think," she answered with a smile.
translation.kr: "네 — 내일이면요." 그 사람이 웃으며 답했네.

translation.en: Tomorrow! How I felt that word.
translation.kr: 내일이라니! 그 말이 내게 어떻게 들렸는지.

translation.en: Ah, she little knew, as she drew her hand away from mine.
translation.kr: 아, 내 손에서 제 손을 빼면서 그 사람은 알지 못했네.

translation.en: They walked down the avenue.
translation.kr: 두 사람은 오솔길을 내려갔네.

translation.en: I stood gazing after them in the moonlight.
translation.kr: 나는 달빛 속에서 그 뒷모습을 바라보며 서 있었네.

translation.en: I threw myself on the ground and wept; then sprang up and ran out onto the terrace, and saw, in the shade of the linden-trees, her white dress disappearing near the garden gate.
translation.kr: 땅에 몸을 던지고 울다가, 벌떡 일어나 테라스로 달려 나가, 보리수 그늘 아래 뜰 문 가까이에서 그 흰옷이 사라지는 것을 보았네.

translation.en: I stretched out my arms, and she was gone.
translation.kr: 나는 두 팔을 뻗었고, 그 사람은 사라지고 없었네.
